models.name: Qwen3.8-27B
models.why: Qwen3.8-27B at 71.6 tok/s on one RTX 5090 with vLLM switched to the Humming kernels (+26% over the kernel vLLM picks by default on that card), 73.1 tok/s on code with Mia's EXL3 4.0bpw + MTP kit on 2x RTX 5060 Ti, and TensorFold 1.1.4 taking CUDA prefill on a GB10 from 203 to 1,045 tok/s at 64K context while decode moves ~2%.

engines.quant: 4-bit NVFP4 with vLLM 0.32.0's --linear-backend humming; one request, up from 56.9 tok/s on vLLM's default kernel for this card
engines.engine_min_version: vLLM 0.32.0 --linear-backend humming (Humming ships inside 0.32.0; do not upgrade humming-kernels on its own, 0.1.18 fails to load dense models there)

engines.quant: EXL3 4.0 bpw with MTP (Mia's kit); code workload, 262K context
SLQ-EAR98 on vLLM (Benjamin Marie's quant); code workload, 94K context
qwen3.8-27b; this is COLD PREFILL (prompt processing at 64K on CUDA) up from 203 tok/s in TensorFold 1.1.3, while decode improved only about 2%

models.name: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
models.why: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on a CPU-only box: llama.cpp 3.47 tok/s with the Bolt drafter off, against Ollama's default drafter slowing the same machine to 1.34 tok/s (+1.7 GiB RSS).

engines.quant: Bolt model, llama.cpp with the drafter disabled

models.name: Gemma 4 E2B
models.why: Gemma 4 E2B on a Raspberry Pi 5 CPU via LiteRT: 9 tok/s decode (99 tok/s prefill) at 1432 MB peak memory.

engines.quant: Gemma 4 E2B on LiteRT-LM; 1432 MB peak memory; 99 tokens/sec prefill (prompt processing, not decode)

models.name: DeepSeek R1 1.5B
models.why: DeepSeek R1 1.5B served by Ollama on a Raspberry Pi 4B with 2GB of LPDDR4, fully offline: 4 tokens per second on CPU.

models.name: LFM2.5-24B-A2B
models.why: Liquid AI's LFM2.5-24B-A2B still leads the tool-use and agent benchmarks it was launched into, at 184 tok/s on an M5 Max (4-bit, 14.5GB).

engines.quant: Liquid AI's compressed 4-bit build, 14.5GB; restatement of the vendor day-1 figure

models.name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 125B
models.why: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on a 48 GB M5 Pro with a 33 GB memory budget: Slotstream held 20.91 to 23.69 tok/s across short prompts, long prompts and coding tasks, while a base M2 Mac mini whose disk reads 1.5 GB/s managed 1.41 tok/s.

engines.hardware: Apple M5 Pro, 48GB unified memory (33GB memory budget)
engines.quant: Slotstream, long-prompt run; the same report measured 20.91 to 23.69 tok/s across short prompts, long prompts and coding tasks

engines.hardware: base Mac mini M2, disk reads 1.5 GB/s
engines.quant: Slotstream, storage-bound run; the same build on an M5 Pro at 17.3 GB/s disk did 20.91 to 23.69 tok/s, and a 32K prompt on a 16GB Mac means over 6 minutes of waiting by the author's estimate
engines.storage_offload: disk reads 1.5 GB/s (M2 Mac mini) vs 17.3 GB/s on the M5 Pro

models.name: Ternary Bonsai 2 27B
models.why: Ternary Bonsai 2 27B on a 48GB M4 Pro MacBook Pro: 120 tok/s on an RTX 5090 against 28 tok/s on an Apple M5 Pro for the same ternary model.

engines.quant: Ternary Bonsai 2 27B reported as the same ternary model run on an RTX 5090 (120 tok/s) and an Apple M5 Pro (28 tok/s)
